links.comparator_used: Adding universal biweekly screening to existing protocols (uniform screening allocation), in an individual-based model calibrated to an Italian pediatric hospital
links.outcome: Incidence of MRSA colonizations versus number of screening tests
links.effect: Biweekly screening reduced colonization incidence by about 33% with a 56% increase in screening tests; ML-targeted screening achieved comparable reductions with only a 20% additional screening effort.
links.tradeoff: Targeted screening still required about 20% more screening tests than existing protocols. Results come from a simulation model, not a prospective trial.
links.quote: However, a targeted screening of patients selected by a trained machine learning classifier would achieve comparable reductions with only a 20% additional screening effort.
